G3800.b:
**† ⟪ὄψώνιον⟫, -ου, τό
(< ὄψον—v.s. ὀψάριον—and ὠνέομαι), [in LXX: I Es 4:56, I Mac 3:28 14:32*;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪provisions⟫, ⟪provision-money⟫, ⟪soldiers' pay⟫: ⟦Luke 3:14|Lk 3:14⟧, ⟦1 Corinthians 9:7|I Co 9:7⟧.
⟪2.⟫ Generally, ⟪wages⟫, ⟪hire⟫: ⟦2 Corinthians 11:8|II Co 11:8⟧; ὄ. τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ⟦Romans 6:23|Ro 6:23⟧ (v. Deiss, BS, 148, 266).†

G3802.b:
† ⟪παγιδεύω⟫
(< παγίς), [in LXX: ⟦1 Samuel 28:9|I Ki 28:9⟧ (⁨נקשׁ⁩ hith.), ⟦Ecclesiastes 9:12|Ec 9:12⟧ (⁨יקשׁ⁩ pu.)*;] ⟪to ensnare⟫: metaph., c. acc., ἐν λόγῳ, ⟦Matthew 22:15|Mt 22:15⟧ (not elsewhere).†

G3803.b:
⟪παγίς⟫, -ίδος, ἡ
(< πήγνυμι), [in LXX for ⁨פַּח⁩, ⁨מוֹקֵשׁ⁩, ⁨רֶשֶׁת⁩, etc.;] poët. (Aristoph., al.) and late for πάγη, ⟪a trap⟫, ⟪snare⟫; metaph. (as also in cl.): ⟦Luke 21:35|Lk 21:35⟧, ⟦Romans 11:9|Ro 11:9⟧(LXX), ⟦1 Timothy 3:7|I Ti 3:7⟧ ⟦1 Timothy 6:9|6:9⟧, ⟦2 Timothy 2:26|II Ti 2:26⟧.†

G3804.b:
* ⟪πάθημα⟫, -τος, τό
(< πάσχω), like πάθος,
⟪1.⟫ ⟪that which befalls one⟫, ⟪a suffering⟫, ⟪affliction⟫: pl., ⟦Romans 8:18|Ro 8:18⟧, ⟦2 Corinthians 1:6|II Co 1:6⟧, ⟦2 Corinthians 1:7|7⟧, ⟦Colossians 1:24|Col 1:24⟧, ⟦2 Timothy 3:11|II Ti 3:11⟧, ⟦Hebrews 2:10|He 2:10⟧ ⟦Hebrews 10:32|10:32⟧, ⟦1 Peter 5:9|I Pe 5:9⟧; of Christ's sufferings: τὰ εἰς Χ., ⟦1 Peter 1:11|I Pe 1:11⟧; τ. Χριστσῦ, ⟦1 Peter 5:1|I Pe 5:1⟧; id. as shared by Christians, ⟦2 Corinthians 1:5|II Co 1:5⟧, ⟦Philippians 3:10|Phl 3:10⟧, ⟦1 Peter 4:13|I Pe 4:13⟧.
⟪2.⟫ ⟪a passive emotion⟫, ⟪affection⟫, ⟪passion⟫: ⟦Galatians 5:24|Ga 5:24⟧; τ. ἁμαρτιῶν, ⟦Romans 7:5|Ro 7:5⟧.
⟪3.⟫ = τὸ πάσχειν, ⟪an enduring⟫ or ⟪suffering⟫: c. gen. obj., ⟦Hebrews 2:9|He 2:9⟧.†
SYN.: v.s. πάθος.

G3805.b:
* ⟪παθητός⟫, -ή, -όν
(< πάσχω),
⟪1.⟫ ⟪one who has suffered⟫.
⟪2.⟫ ⟪subject to suffering⟫ (R, mg., v. M, Pr., 222) or ⟪destined to suffer⟫ (AV, R, txt.): ⟦Acts 26:23|Ac 26:23⟧.†
a: A Grammar of N.T. Greek. Vol. I, Prolegomena, by J. H. Moulton. Third Edition. Scribners, 1908

G3806.b:
⟪πάθος⟫, -ους, τό
(< πάσχω), [in LXX: ⟦Job 30:31|Jb 30:31⟧ (⁨אֵבֶל⁩), ⟦Proverbs 25:20|Pr 25:20⟧, and very freq. in IV Mac (1:1 ff., al.)*;] like πάθημα;
⟪1.⟫ ⟪that which befalls one⟫, ⟪that which one suffers⟫.
⟪2.⟫ ⟪a passive emotion⟫ or ⟪affection⟫ (esp. of violent emotion), ⟪a passion⟫, ⟪passionate desire⟫; in NT always in bad sense: ⟦Colossians 3:5|Col 3:5⟧; π. ἀτιμίας, ⟦Romans 1:26|Ro 1:26⟧; π. ἐπιθυμίας, ⟦1 Thessalonians 4:5|I Th 4:5⟧.†
SYN.: π. = πάθημα, exc. that πάθημα is the more concrete and particular. In NT usage, π. represents the passive, ungoverned aspect of evil desire, as opp. to ἐπιθυμία, which is the active and also the more comprehensive term (v. Tr., Syn., lxxxvii); cf. also ὄρεξις.
a: Synonyms of the N. T. , by R. C. Trench. Ninth Edition. Macmillan, 1880

G3807.b:
* ⟪παιδαγωγός⟫, -οῦ, ὁ
(< παῖς, ἄγω), a guide, guardian, trainer of boys, ⟪a tutor⟫ (disting. from διδάσκαλος, Xen., Lac., 3, 1), usually a trusty slave: opp. to πατήρ, ⟦1 Corinthians 4:15|I Co 4:15⟧; fig., of the Law, π. εἰς Χριστόν, ⟦Galatians 3:24|Ga 3:24⟧, ⟦Galatians 3:25|25⟧.†

G3808.b:
⟪παιδάριον⟫, -ου, τό, dimin. of παῖς,
[in LXX chiefly for ⁨נַעַר⁩;] ⟪a little boy⟫, ⟪a lad⟫ (in late and colloq. Gk. the word seems to be used with greater latitude and even to lose its dimin. force entirely; cf. To 6:2, 3, and v. MM, xviii): ⟦John 6:9|Jo 6:9⟧.†
SYN.: v.s. παῖς.

G3809.b:
⟪παιδεία⟫ (-ία, T), -ας, ἡ
(< παιδεύω), [in LXX chiefly for ⁨מוּסָר⁩;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪the rearing of a child⟫ (Æsch.).
⟪2.⟫ ⟪training⟫, ⟪learning⟫, ⟪instruction⟫ (Plat., al.): ⟦Ephesians 6:4|Eph 6:4⟧, ⟦2 Timothy 3:16|II Ti 3:16⟧.
⟪3.⟫ As in LXX (⟦Proverbs 3:11|Pr 3:11⟧ ⟦Proverbs 15:5|15:5⟧, al.), ⟪chastening⟫, ⟪discipline⟫: ⟦Hebrews 12:5|He 12:5⟧(LXX), ⟦Hebrews 12:7|7⟧, ⟦Hebrews 12:8|8⟧, ⟦Hebrews 12:11|11⟧.†

G3810.b:
⟪παιδευτής⟫, -οῦ, ὁ
(< παιδεύω), [in LXX: ⟦Hosea 5:2|Ho 5:2⟧ (⁨מוּסָר⁩), Si 37:19, IV Mac 5:34 9:6*;]
⟪1.⟫ prop., ⟪a teacher⟫, ⟪instructor⟫: ⟦Romans 2:20|Ro 2:20⟧.
⟪2.⟫ ⟪a corrector⟫, ⟪one who disciplines⟫ (cf. ⟦Hosea 5:2|Ho 5:2⟧): ⟦Hebrews 12:9|He 12:9⟧.†

G3811.b:
⟪παιδεύω⟫
(< παίς), [in LXX chiefly for ⁨יסר⁩;]
⟪1.⟫ as in cl., ⟪to train children⟫, hence, generally, ⟪to teach⟫, ⟪instruct⟫: ⟦Acts 7:22|Ac 7:22⟧ ⟦Acts 22:3|22:3⟧, ⟦1 Timothy 1:20|I Ti 1:20⟧, ⟦Titus 2:12|Tit 2:12⟧.
⟪2.⟫ As in LXX (⟦Psalms 6:2|Ps 6:2⟧, ⟦Proverbs 19:18|Pr 19:18⟧, Wi 3:5, al., and for prob. ex. from π., v. MM, xviii), ⟪to chasten⟫, ⟪correct⟫, ⟪chastise⟫: ⟦Luke 23:16|Lk 23:16⟧, ⟦Luke 23:22|22⟧, ⟦2 Timothy 2:25|II Ti 2:25⟧, ⟦Hebrews 12:7|He 12:7⟧, ⟦Hebrews 12:10|10⟧; of divine chastening, ⟦1 Corinthians 11:32|I Co 11:32⟧, ⟦2 Corinthians 6:9|II Co 6:9⟧, ⟦Hebrews 12:6|He 12:6⟧, ⟦Revelation 3:19|Re 3:19⟧.†
SYN.: διδάσκω, q.v.

G3812.b:
⟪παιδιόθεν⟫
(< παιδίον), adv.,
[in LXX: ⟦Genesis 47:3|Ge 47:3⟧*;] = cl. ἐκ παιδός, παιδίου, ⟪from childhood⟫: ⟦Mark 9:21|Mk 9:21⟧.†

G3813.b:
⟪παιδίον⟫, -ου, τό,
dimin, of παῖς, [in LXX chiefly for ⁨יֶלֶד⁩, also for ⁨נַעַר⁩, ⁨בֵּן⁩, etc., freq. in To in ref. to full-grown youth;] ⟪a young child⟫, ⟪a little one⟫: ⟦Matthew 2:8|Mt 2:8⟧, ⟦Matthew 2:9|9⟧, ⟦Matthew 2:11|11⟧, ff., ⟦Luke 1:59|Lk 1:59⟧, ⟦Luke 1:66|66⟧, ⟦Luke 1:76|76⟧, ⟦Luke 1:80|80⟧ ⟦Luke 2:17|2:17⟧, ⟦Luke 2:27|27⟧, ⟦Luke 2:40|40⟧, ⟦John 16:21|Jo 16:21⟧, ⟦Hebrews 11:23|He 11:23⟧; of older children, ⟦Matthew 18:2|Mt 18:2⟧, ⟦Matthew 18:4|4⟧, ⟦Matthew 18:5|5⟧, ⟦Mark 5:39|Mk 5:39-41⟧ ⟦Mark 7:30|7:30⟧ ⟦Mark 9:24|9:24⟧, ⟦Mark 9:36|36⟧, ⟦Luke 9:47|Lk 9:47⟧, ⟦Luke 9:48|48⟧ ⟦Luke 18:17|18:17⟧, ⟦John 4:49|Jo 4:49⟧; in pl., ⟦Matthew 11:16|Mt 11:16⟧ ⟦Matthew 14:21|14:21⟧ ⟦Matthew 15:38|15:38⟧ ⟦Matthew 18:3|18:3⟧ ⟦Matthew 19:13|19:13⟧, ⟦Matthew 19:14|14⟧, ⟦Mark 7:28|Mk 7:28⟧ ⟦Mark 10:13|10:13⟧ ff., ⟦Luke 7:32|Lk 7:32⟧ ⟦Luke 11:7|11:7⟧ ⟦Luke 18:16|18:16⟧, ⟦Hebrews 2:13|He 2:13⟧, ⟦Hebrews 2:14|14⟧ Metaph., ⟦1 Corinthians 14:20|I Co 14:20⟧. Colloq. in familiar address (as Eng. colloq., "lads"—v. M, Pr., 170n—and Irish use of "boys"): ⟦John 21:5|Jo 21:5⟧, ⟦1 John 2:13|I Jo 2:13⟧, ⟦1 John 2:18|18⟧ ⟦1 John 3:7|3:7⟧.†
SYN.: v.s. παῖς.
a: A Grammar of N.T. Greek. Vol. I, Prolegomena, by J. H. Moulton. Third Edition. Scribners, 1908

G3814.b:
⟪παιδίσκη⟫, -ης, ἡ,
dimin, of παῖς, [in LXX for ⁨שִׁפְחָה⁩, ⁨אָמָה⁩, etc.;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪a young girl⟫, ⟪a maiden⟫ (⁨נַעֲרָה⁩, ⟦Ruth 4:12|Ru 4:12⟧).
⟪2.⟫ Colloq., ⟪a young female slave⟫, ⟪a maid-servant⟫ (v. Kennedy, Sources, 40 f.; Deiss., LAE, 186, 3322): ⟦Matthew 26:69|Mt 26:69⟧, ⟦Mark 14:66|Mk 14:66⟧, ⟦Mark 14:69|69⟧, ⟦Luke 12:45|Lk 12:45⟧ ⟦Luke 22:56|22:56⟧, ⟦John 18:17|Jo 18:17⟧, ⟦Acts 12:13|Ac 12:13⟧ ⟦Acts 16:16|16:16⟧; of Hagar, ⟦Galatians 4:22|Ga 4:22⟧, ⟦Galatians 4:23|23⟧, ⟦Galatians 4:30|30⟧(LXX); id., metaph., ⟦Galatians 4:31|Ga 4:31⟧.†
SYN.: v.s. παῖς.
a: Light from the Ancient East, by A. Deissmann, tr. by L. R. M. Strachan. Second Edition. Hodder, 1908
Sources of N.T. Greek, by H. A. A. Kennedy. T. & T. Clark, 1895

G3815.b:
⟪παίζω⟫
(< παῖς), [in LXX: ⟦Genesis 21:9|Ge 21:9⟧ ⟦Genesis 26:8|26:8⟧, ⟦Exodus 32:6|Ex 32:6⟧ (⁨צחק⁩ pi.); and more freq. (⟦Judges 16:25|Jg 16:25⟧, al.) for (⁨שׁחק⁩ pi.;] prop., ⟪to play as a child⟫, hence, generally, ⟪to play⟫ (as with singing and dancing): ⟦1 Corinthians 10:7|I Co 10:7⟧(LXX) (cf. ἐμ-παίζω).†

G3816.b:
⟪παῖς⟫, gen., παιδός, ὁ, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for ⁨עֶבֶד⁩, also for ⁨נַעַר⁩, ⁨נַעֲרָה⁩, etc.;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪a child, boy⟫, ⟪youth⟫, ⟪maiden⟫: ὁ π., ⟦Matthew 17:18|Mt 17:18⟧, ⟦Luke 2:43|Lk 2:43⟧ ⟦Luke 9:42|9:42⟧, ⟦Acts 20:12|Ac 20:12⟧; ἡ π. ⟦Luke 8:51|Lk 8:51⟧, ⟦Luke 8:54|54⟧ (on the artic. nom, of address, v. M, Pr., 70 f., 235; Bl., § 33, 4); pl., ⟦Matthew 2:16|Mt 2:16⟧ ⟦Matthew 21:15|21:15⟧; of parentage, c. gen., ⟦John 4:51|Jo 4:51⟧.
⟪2.⟫ Like Heb. ⁨עֶבֶד⁩, Lat. puer, Fr. garçon, Eng. ⟪boy⟫ (Æsch., Aristoph., Xen., al.), ⟪servant⟫, ⟪slave⟫, ⟪attendant⟫: ⟦Matthew 8:6|Mt 8:6⟧, ⟦Matthew 8:8|8⟧, ⟦Matthew 8:13|13⟧, ⟦Luke 7:7|Lk 7:7⟧ ⟦Luke 12:45|12:45⟧ ⟦Luke 15:26|15:26⟧; in late writers (Diod., LXX: ⟦Genesis 41:37|Ge 41:37⟧, al.), of a king's attendant or minister: ⟦Matthew 14:2|Mt 14:2⟧; so (= Heb. ⁨עֶבֶד⁩ ⁨יְהֹוָה⁩) π. τ. θεοῦ (⟦Psalms 69:18|Ps 66 (69):18⟧, ⟦Isaiah 41:8|Is 41:8⟧, Wi 2:13, al.), of Israel, ⟦Luke 1:54|Lk 1:54⟧; of David, ⟦Luke 1:69|Lk 1:69⟧, ⟦Acts 4:25|Ac 4:25⟧; of Jesus (but v. Dalman, Words, 277 f.), ⟦Matthew 12:18|Mt 12:18⟧(LXX), ⟦Acts 3:13|Ac 3:13⟧, ⟦Acts 3:26|26⟧ ⟦Acts 4:27|4:27⟧, ⟦Acts 4:30|30⟧.†
SYN.: 1. τέκνον, child, with emphasis on parentage and the consequent community of nature; υἱός, son, with emphasis on the privileged position of heirship; π. refers both to age and parentage, but with emphasis on the former. Cf. also παιδάριον, παιδίον, παιδίσκη, and v. Westc. on ⟦1 John 3:1|I Jo 3:1⟧. 2. v.s. θεράπων, and cf. Thackeray, Gr., 7 f.
a: The Words of Jesus, by G. Dalman. English Edition. T. & T. Clark, 1902
A Grammar of N.T. Greek. Vol. I, Prolegomena, by J. H. Moulton. Third Edition. Scribners, 1908
A Grammar of the O.T. in Greek I, by H. St. J. Thackeray. Cambridge, 1909
Commentaries on the Gospel according to St. John, by B. F. Westcott, 2 Vols., Murray, 1908; the Epistle to the Ephesians, Macmiilan, 1906; the Epistles of St. John, Third Edition, Macmillan, 1892

G3817.b:
⟪παίω⟫,
[in LXX chiefly for ⁨נכה⁩ hi.;] ⟪to strike⟫, ⟪smite⟫: with the hand or fist, ⟦Matthew 26:68|Mt 26:68⟧, ⟦Luke 22:64|Lk 22:64⟧; with a sword, ⟦Mark 14:47|Mk 14:47⟧, ⟦John 18:10|Jo 18:10⟧; of a reptile, ⟪to sting⟫: ⟦Revelation 9:5|Re 9:5⟧.†

G3818.b: ⟪Πακατιανή⟫, -ῆς, ἡ, ⟪Pacatiana⟫, the Western part of the Province of Phrygia, as constituted in iv/A.D.: 1Ti subscr. (Rec.).†

G3819.b:
⟪πάλαι⟫, adv. of time,
[in LXX: ⟦Isaiah 48:5|Is 48:5⟧, ⟦Isaiah 48:7|7⟧ (⁨מֵאָז⁩), etc.;] ⟪long ago⟫, ⟪of old⟫, ⟪in time past⟫ (denoting past time absolutely, as πρότερον relatively): ⟦Matthew 11:21|Mt 11:21⟧, ⟦Luke 10:13|Lk 10:13⟧, ⟦Hebrews 1:1|He 1:1⟧, ⟦Jude 1:4|Ju 4⟧; as adj., c. art., ⟦2 Peter 1:9|II Pe 1:9⟧; of time just past, ⟦Mark 6:47|Mk 6:47⟧ (WH, mg.), ⟦Mark 15:44|15:44⟧ (WH, mg., R, txt.); c. durat. praes. (RV, all this time), ⟦2 Corinthians 12:19|II Co 12:19⟧.†
a: The N.T. in the original Greek, by B. F. Westcott and F. J. A. Hort. Vol. II, Introduction and Appendix. Macmillan, 1881

G3820.b:
⟪παλαιός⟫, -ά, -όν
(< πάλαι), [in LXX: ⟦Leviticus 25:22|Le 25:22⟧ ⟦Leviticus 26:10|26:10⟧, ⟦Song of Solomon 7:13|Ca 7:13⟧ (⟦Song of Solomon 7:14|14⟧) (⁨ישׁן⁩), ⟦Joshua 9:4|Jos 9:4⟧, ⟦Joshua 9:5|5⟧, ⟦Jeremiah 38:11|Je 45 (38):11⟧ (⁨בָּלֶה⁩), etc.;] ⟪old⟫, ⟪ancient⟫; opp. to νέος, καινός: οἶνος, ⟦Luke 5:39|Lk 5:39⟧; διαθήκη, ⟦2 Corinthians 3:14|II Co 3:14⟧; ἐντολή, ⟦1 John 2:7|I Jo 2:7⟧; ζύμη, ⟦1 Corinthians 5:7|I Co 5:7⟧, ⟦1 Corinthians 5:8|8⟧; ὁ π. ἄςθρωπος (for similar phrases, v. Westc., Eph., 68), ⟦Romans 6:6|Ro 6:6⟧, ⟦Ephesians 4:22|Eph 4:22⟧, ⟦Colossians 3:9|Col 3:9⟧; neut. pl., καινὰ καὶ π., ⟦Matthew 13:52|Mt 13:52⟧; of things not merely old, but worn by use (as ⟦Joshua 9:4|Jos 9:4⟧, ⟦Joshua 9:5|5⟧, LXX), ⟦Matthew 9:16|Mt 9:16⟧, ⟦Matthew 9:17|17⟧, ⟦Mark 2:21|Mk 2:21⟧, ⟦Mark 2:22|22⟧, ⟦Luke 5:36|Lk 5:36⟧, ⟦Luke 5:37|37⟧.†
SYN.: v.s. ἀρχαῖος.
a: Commentaries on the Gospel according to St. John, by B. F. Westcott, 2 Vols., Murray, 1908; the Epistle to the Ephesians, Macmiilan, 1906; the Epistles of St. John, Third Edition, Macmillan, 1892

G3822.b:
⟪παλαιόω⟫, -ῶ
(< παλαιός), [in LXX chiefly for ⁨בּלה⁩, pi., in pass. for ⁨בּ׳⁩ qal.;] ⟪to make⟫ or ⟪declare old⟫: ⟦Hebrews 8:13|He 8:13⟧; pass., ⟪to become old⟫: of things worn out by time and use (cf. ⟦John 9:13|Jo 9:13⟧, ⟦Isaiah 50:9|Is 50:9⟧, al., and v.s. παλαιός), ⟦Luke 12:33|Lk 12:33⟧, ⟦Hebrews 1:11|He 1:11⟧(LXX); τὸ παλαιούμενον, ⟦Hebrews 8:13|He 8:13⟧ (where this and the act., v. supr., may have the sense of abrogate, v. LS, Zorell, s.v.).†
SYN.: γηράσκω.
a: A Greek-English Lexicon, by H. G. Liddell and R. Scott. Seventh Edition. Harper, 1889
Novi Testamenti Lexicon Graecum (Cursus Scripturae Sacrae I, vii), auctore Fr, Zorell, S.J. Paris, 1911

G3823.b:
* ⟪πάλη⟫, -ης, ἡ
(< πάλλω, to sway) ⟪wrestling⟫, hence, generally, ⟪fight⟫, contest: fig., of the spiritual combat of Christians, ⟦Ephesians 6:12|Eph 6:12⟧.†

G3825.b:
⟪πάλιν⟫, adv.,
[in LXX for ⁨שׁוּב⁩, etc.;]
⟪1.⟫ of place, ⟪back⟫, ⟪backwards⟫ (LS, s.v.).
⟪2.⟫ Of time, ⟪again⟫, ⟪once more⟫: ⟦Matthew 4:8|Mt 4:8⟧, ⟦Mark 2:13|Mk 2:13⟧, ⟦Luke 23:20|Lk 23:20⟧, ⟦John 1:35|Jo 1:35⟧ (and freq.), ⟦Acts 17:32|Ac 17:32⟧, ⟦Romans 11:23|Ro 11:23⟧, ⟦Galatians 1:9|Ga 1:9⟧, ⟦Hebrews 1:6|He 1:6⟧, al; pleonastically, π. ἀνακάμπτειν, ⟦Acts 18:21|Ac 18:21⟧; ὑποστρέφειν, ⟦Galatians 1:17|Ga 1:17⟧; εἰς τὸ π., ⟦2 Corinthians 13:2|II Co 13:2⟧; π. ἐκ τρίτου (Bl., § 81, 4), ⟦Matthew 26:44|Mt 26:44⟧; ἐκ δευτέρου, ⟦Matthew 26:42|Mt 26:42⟧, ⟦Acts 10:15|Ac 10:15⟧; π. δεῦτερον, ⟦John 4:54|Jo 4:54⟧ ⟦John 21:16|21:16⟧; π. ἄνωθεν ( Wi 19:6), ⟦Galatians 4:9|Ga 4:9⟧.
⟪3.⟫ Rhetorically, ⟪again⟫;
	⟪(a)⟫ ⟪further⟫, ⟪moreover⟫: ⟦Matthew 5:33|Mt 5:33⟧, ⟦Luke 13:20|Lk 13:20⟧, ⟦John 12:39|Jo 12:39⟧, al.;
	⟪(b)⟫ ⟪in turn⟫, ⟪on the other hand⟫ (Soph.; LXX: Wi 13:8 16:23, al.): ⟦Luke 6:43|Lk 6:43⟧, ⟦1 Corinthians 12:21|I Co 12:21⟧, ⟦2 Corinthians 10:7|II Co 10:7⟧, ⟦1 John 2:8|I Jo 2:8⟧.
a: A Greek-English Lexicon, by H. G. Liddell and R. Scott. Seventh Edition. Harper, 1889
The Words of Jesus, by G. Dalman. English Edition. T. & T. Clark, 1902
Commentary on St. Paul's Epistles, by C. J. Ellicott. Andover, 1860-65

G3827.b:
** ⟪πάμπολυς⟫, -πόλλη, -πολυ
(< πᾶς, πολύς), [in Sm.: ⟦Job 36:31|Jb 36:31⟧, ⟦Psalms 40:6|Ps 39 (40):6⟧ ⟦Psalms 89:51|88 (89):51⟧*;] ⟪very much⟫, ⟪very great⟫: ⟦Mark 8:1|Mk 8:1⟧, Rec. (RV, Edd., πάλιν πολλοῦ).†

G3828.b: ⟪Παμφυλία⟫, -ας, ἡ, ⟪Pamphylia⟫, a province of Asia Minor: ⟦Acts 2:10|Ac 2:10⟧ ⟦Acts 13:13|13:13⟧ ⟦Acts 14:24|14:24⟧ ⟦Acts 15:38|15:38⟧ ⟦Acts 27:5|27:5⟧.†

G3829.b:

(< πανδοχεύς), late form of Att. πανδοκεῖον, ⟪an inn⟫ (khân, caravanserai): ⟦Luke 10:34|Lk 10:34⟧.†

G3830.b:
* ⟪παν-δοχεύς⟫, -έως, ὁ
(< πᾶς, δέχομαι), late form of the Att. πανδοκεύς (T, in l.), ⟪an innkeeper⟫, ⟪host⟫: ⟦Luke 10:35|Lk 10:35⟧.†

G3831.b:
⟪πανήγυρις⟫, -εως, ἡ
(< πᾶς + ἄγυρας = ἀγορά), [in LXX: ⟦Hosea 2:11|Ho 2:11⟧ (⟦Hosea 2:13|13⟧) 9:5, ⟦Ezekiel 46:11|Ez 46:11⟧ (⁨מוֹעֵד⁩), ⟦Amos 5:21|Am 5:21⟧ (⁨עֲצָרָה⁩)*;] prop., ⟪a national festal assembly⟫ in honour of a god; hence, generally, any ⟪festal assembly⟫: ⟦Hebrews 12:23|He 12:23⟧ (for exx. in π., v. MM, xviii).†
SYN.: ἐκκλησία (q.v.), συναγωγή.

G3832.b:
⟪πανοικεί⟫ (Rec., LTr., -κί), adv.
(< πᾶς, οἶκος), a word rejected by strict Atticists, though found once in Plat. (Eryx., 392 c); [in LXX: ⟦Exodus 1:1|Ex 1:1⟧ (⁨בַּיִת⁩), III Mac 3:27 (where A in each case reads -κίᾳ, the Attic form, cf. ⟦Genesis 50:8|Ge 50:8⟧, al.)*;] ⟪with all the household⟫: ⟦Acts 16:34|Ac 16:34⟧.†

G3833.b:
⟪πανοπλία⟫, -ας, ἡ
(< πᾶς, ὅπλον), [in LXX: ⟦2 Samuel 2:21|II Ki 2:21⟧ (⁨חֲלִיצָה⁩), ⟦Job 39:20|Jb 39:20⟧, Jth 14:3, Wi 5:17, Si 46:6, I, II, IV Mac6*;] ⟪full armour⟫: ⟦Luke 11:22|Lk 11:22⟧; metaph. (cf. Wi 5:17), τ. θεοῦ, ⟦Ephesians 6:11|Eph 6:11⟧, ⟦Ephesians 6:13|13⟧.†

G3834.b:
⟪πανουργία⟫, -ας, ἡ
(< πανοῦργος), [in LXX: ⟦Joshua 9:4|Jos 9:4⟧, ⟦Proverbs 1:4|Pr 1:4⟧ ⟦Proverbs 8:5|8:5⟧ (⁨עׇרְמָה⁩), ⟦Numbers 24:22|Nu 24:22⟧, Si 19:25 21:22 31 (34):10 (in all cases in good or indifferent sense)*;] ⟪cleverness⟫, in cl. nearly always in bad sense, ⟪craftiness⟫, ⟪cunning⟫, ⟪knavery⟫: ⟦Luke 20:23|Lk 20:23⟧, ⟦1 Corinthians 3:19|I Co 3:19⟧ (LXX, φρόνησις, for ⁨עׇרְמָה⁩) ⟦2 Corinthians 4:2|II Co 4:2⟧ ⟦2 Corinthians 11:3|11:3⟧, ⟦Ephesians 4:14|Eph 4:14⟧.†

G3826.b:
*† ⟪πανπληθεί⟫ (Rec. παμπλ-, v. WH, App., 150), adv.
(< πᾶς, πλῆθος), = cl. παμπληθές, ⟪with the whole multitude⟫, ⟪all together⟫: ⟦Luke 23:18|Lk 23:18⟧.†
a: The N.T. in the original Greek, by B. F. Westcott and F. J. A. Hort. Vol. II, Introduction and Appendix. Macmillan, 1881

G3836.b:
⟪πανταχόθεν⟫, adv.,
[in LXX: IV Mac 13:1 15:32*;] ⟪from all sides⟫: ⟦Mark 1:45|Mk 1:45⟧, Rec.†

G3838.b:
** ⟪παντελής⟫, -ές
(< πᾶς, τέλος), [in LXX: III Mac 7:16 A*;] ⟪all-complete⟫, ⟪entire⟫, ⟪perfect⟫; εἰς τ. παντελές, ⟪completely⟫, ⟪utterly⟫: ⟦Luke 13:11|Lk 13:11⟧, ⟦Hebrews 7:25|He 7:25⟧ (where perhaps in temp. sense, finally; v. MM, xviii).†

G3839.b:
** ⟪πάντῃ⟫ (Rec. -τη), adv.
(< πᾶς), [in LXX: Si 50:22, III Mac 4:1*;] ⟪every way⟫, ⟪entirely⟫: ⟦Acts 24:3|Ac 24:3⟧.†

G3840.b:
⟪πάντοθεν⟫, adv.
(< πᾶς), [in LXX: ⟦Jeremiah 48:31|Je 31 (48):31⟧ (⁨כֻּלֹּה⁩), al.;] ⟪from all sides⟫: ⟦Mark 1:45|Mk 1:45⟧, ⟦Luke 19:43|Lk 19:43⟧, ⟦Hebrews 9:4|He 9:4⟧.†

G3841.b:
† ⟪παντοκράτωρ⟫, -ορος, ὁ
(< πᾶς, κρατέω), [in LXX: freq. in ⟦Job 5:8|Jb 5:8⟧, ⟦Job 5:17|17⟧, al. (⁨שַׁדַּי⁩), and for ⁨צְבָאוֹת⁩, in the phrase θεός (κυρίος) π., ⟦2 Samuel 5:10|II Ki 5:10⟧, al., and freq. in Am, Za, Ma; also in Wi 7:25, Si 42:17 50:14, 17, and freq. in Jth, II, III Mac;] ⟪almighty⟫: ⟦2 Corinthians 6:18|II Co 6:18⟧, ⟦Revelation 1:8|Re 1:8⟧ ⟦Revelation 4:8|4:8⟧ ⟦Revelation 11:17|11:17⟧ ⟦Revelation 15:3|15:3⟧ ⟦Revelation 16:7|16:7⟧, ⟦Revelation 16:14|14⟧ ⟦Revelation 19:6|19:6⟧, ⟦Revelation 9:15|15⟧ ⟦Revelation 21:22|21:22⟧.†

G3842.b:

(< πᾶς), [in LXX: Wi 11:21 19:18*;] in late writers (once in Arist.) for διαπαντός, ἑκάστοτε, ⟪at all times⟫, ⟪always⟫: ⟦Matthew 26:11|Mt 26:11⟧, ⟦Mark 14:7|Mk 14:7⟧, ⟦Luke 15:31|Lk 15:31⟧, ⟦John 6:34|Jo 6:34⟧, ⟦Romans 1:10|Ro 1:10⟧, and freq. in Paul. Epp.

G3845.b:
⟪παρα-βαίνω⟫,
[in LXX for ⁨סוּר⁩, ⁨עבר⁩, ⁨פּרר⁩ hi., ⁨שׂטה⁩, etc.;]
⟪1.⟫ in Hom. (twice), ⟪to go by the side of⟫, ⟪stand beside⟫.
⟪2.⟫ In Æsch., Herod., Thuc., al., ⟪to go past⟫ or ⟪pass over⟫, chiefly metaph., ⟪to overstep⟫, ⟪violate⟫, ⟪transgress⟫ (⟦Joshua 7:11|Jos 7:11⟧, ⟦Ezekiel 16:59|Ez 16:59⟧, Si 40:14, al.): τ. παράδοσιν, ⟦Matthew 15:2|Mt 15:2⟧; τ. ἐντολήν, ⟦Matthew 15:3|Mt 15:3⟧; seq. ἀπό (as ⁨סוּר⁩ ⁨מִן⁩, ⟦Deuteronomy 17:20|De 17:20⟧, al.), ⟪to turn aside⟫, ⟪fall away⟫ (cf. π. τῆς ἀληθείας, Arist., Cael., i, 5, 2): ⟦Acts 1:25|Ac 1:25⟧.†

G3846.b:
⟪παρα-βάλλω⟫,
[in LXX: ⟦Proverbs 2:2|Pr 2:2⟧ ⟦Proverbs 4:20|4:20⟧ ⟦Proverbs 5:1|5:1⟧, ⟦Proverbs 5:13|13⟧ ⟦Proverbs 22:17|22:17⟧ (⁨נטה⁩ hi.), ⟦Ruth 2:16|Ru 2:16⟧ (⁨שׁלל⁩), II Mac 14:38 (elsewhere as v.l.4)*;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪to throw to⟫ or ⟪beside⟫, as fodder to horses (Hom., al.).
⟪2.⟫ ⟪to lay beside⟫, ⟪compare⟫ (Hdt., Plat., al.): ⟦Mark 4:30|Mk 4:30⟧, Rec.
⟪3.⟫ Reflexive, ⟪to betake oneself⟫, ⟪come near⟫; of seamen, ⟪to cross over⟫: εἰς Σάμον, ⟦Acts 20:15|Ac 20:15⟧.
⟪4.⟫ In mid. = παρα-βολεύομαι, q.v.†

G3847.b:
⟪παρά-βασις⟫, -εως, ἡ
(< παραβαίνω), [in LXX: ⟦Psalms 101:3|Ps 100 (101):3⟧ (⁨סֵטִים⁩), ⟦2 Kings 2:24|IV Ki 2:24⟧ A, Wi 14:31, II Mac 15:10*;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪a going aside⟫, ⟪a deviation⟫ (Arist.).
⟪2.⟫ In later writers, ⟪an overstepping⟫; metaph., ⟪transgression⟫ (Plut., al.): ⟦Romans 4:15|Ro 4:15⟧ ⟦Romans 5:14|5:14⟧, ⟦Hebrews 2:2|He 2:2⟧ ⟦Hebrews 9:15|9:15⟧; τ. νόμου, ⟦Romans 2:23|Ro 2:23⟧; ἐν π., ⟦1 Timothy 2:14|I Ti 2:14⟧; τ. παραβάσεων χάριν, ⟦Galatians 3:19|Ga 3:19⟧.
SYN.: v.s. ἁμαρτία.

G3848.b:
** ⟪παρα-βάτης⟫, -ου, ὁ
(< παραβαίνω), [in Sm.: ⟦Psalms 17:4|Ps 16 (17):4⟧ ⟦Psalms 139:19|138 (139):19⟧, ⟦Jeremiah 6:28|Je 6:28⟧*;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪one who stands beside⟫, ⟪the warrior who stands by the charioteer⟫ (cf. παραβαίνω, 1).
⟪2.⟫ ⟪a transgressor⟫ (Æsch., παρβάτης): ⟦Galatians 2:18|Ga 2:18⟧, ⟦James 2:9|Ja 2:9⟧; π. νόμου, ⟦Romans 2:25|Ro 2:25⟧, ⟦Romans 2:27|27⟧, ⟦James 2:11|Ja 2:11⟧.†

G3849.b:
† ⟪παρα-βιάζομαι⟫,
[in LXX: ⟦Genesis 19:9|Ge 19:9⟧, ⟦2 Kings 2:17|IV Ki 2:17⟧ (⁨בְּ׳⁩ ⁨פָּצַר⁩), ⟦Deuteronomy 1:43|De 1:43⟧ (⁨זוּד⁩ hi.), ⟦1 Samuel 28:23|I Ki 28:23⟧ (⁨בְּ׳⁩ ⁨פָּרַץ⁩) v.1.4*;]
⟪1.⟫ prop., ⟪to force against nature⟫ or ⟪law⟫.
⟪2.⟫ ⟪to compel by force⟫ (Polyb.).
⟪3.⟫ ⟪to constrain by entreaty⟫ (⟦Genesis 19:9|Ge 19:9⟧, ⟦1 Samuel 28:23|I Ki 28:23⟧): ⟦Luke 24:29|Lk 24:29⟧, ⟦Acts 16:15|Ac 16:15⟧.†

G3851.b: *† ⟪παρα-βολεύομαι⟫ = cl. παραβάλλομαι (II Mac 14:38), ⟪to expose oneself to danger⟫, ⟪hazard one's life⟫: c. dat. ref., τ. ψυχῇ (v. M, Pr., 64), ⟦Philippians 2:30|Phl 2:30⟧ (Rec. παραβουλ-). Cited by Deiss., LAE, 84, 120.†
a: Light from the Ancient East, by A. Deissmann, tr. by L. R. M. Strachan. Second Edition. Hodder, 1908
A Grammar of N.T. Greek. Vol. I, Prolegomena, by J. H. Moulton. Third Edition. Scribners, 1908

G3850.b:
⟪παραβολή⟫, -ῆς, ἡ
(< παραβάλλω), [in LXX (cf. McNeile, Mt., 185): ⟦Numbers 23:7|Nu 23:7⟧, ⟦Deuteronomy 28:37|De 28:37⟧, ⟦Psalms 44:14|Ps 43 (44):14⟧, ⟦Proverbs 1:6|Pr 1:6⟧, ⟦Ezekiel 12:22|Ez 12:22⟧, al. (⁨מָשָׁל⁩), Si 47:17 (⁨חִידָה⁩), al. mutt. in Si, Wi 5:3;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪a placing beside⟫, ⟪juxtaposition⟫ (Polyb., al.).
⟪2.⟫ ⟪a comparing⟫, ⟪comparison⟫ (Plat., Arist., al.).
⟪3.⟫ ⟪a comparison⟫, ⟪illustration⟫, ⟪analogy⟫, ⟪figure⟫ (Arist., al.): ⟦Matthew 24:32|Mt 24:32⟧, ⟦Mark 3:23|Mk 3:23⟧, ⟦Hebrews 9:9|He 9:9⟧ ⟦Hebrews 11:19|11:19⟧; specif. of the pictures and narratives drawn from nature and human life which are characteristic of the synoptic teaching of our Lord, ⟪a parable⟫: ⟦Matthew 13:3|Mt 13:3⟧, ⟦Matthew 13:10|10⟧, ⟦Mark 4:2|Mk 4:2⟧, ⟦Mark 4:10|10⟧, ⟦Luke 8:4|Lk 8:4⟧, ⟦Luke 8:9|9-11⟧, al.; c. gen. ref., ⟦Matthew 13:18|Mt 13:18⟧, ⟦Matthew 13:36|36⟧.
⟪4⟫ Like Heb. ⁨מָשָׁל⁩ (⟦1 Samuel 10:12|I Ki 10:12⟧, ⟦Proverbs 1:6|Pr 1:6⟧, Si 3:29, al.), = παροιμία, ⟪a proverb⟫ or gnomic saying: ⟦Luke 4:23|Lk 4:23⟧ ⟦Luke 5:36|5:36⟧ ⟦Luke 6:39|6:39⟧.
SYN.: παροιμία (v. Abbott, Essays, 82 ff.).
a: Essays chiefly on the Original Texts of the Old and New Testaments, by T. K. Abbott. Longmans, 1891

G3852.b:
* ⟪παρ-αγγελία⟫, -ας, ἡ
(< παραγγέλλω), ⟪an instruction⟫, ⟪charge⟫, ⟪command⟫: ⟦Acts 5:28|Ac 5:28⟧ ⟦Acts 16:24|16:24⟧, ⟦1 Thessalonians 4:2|I Th 4:2⟧, ⟦1 Timothy 1:5|I Ti 1:5⟧, ⟦1 Timothy 1:18|18⟧. (In Xen., Polyb., of a military order.)†

G3853.b:
⟪παρ-αγγέλλω⟫
(< παρά, ἀγγὲλλω), [in LXX for ⁨שׁמע⁩ pi., hi., etc.;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪to transmit a message⟫ (Æsch., Eur.).
⟪2.⟫ ⟪to order⟫, ⟪command⟫ (Hdt., Xen., al.): c. inf., ⟦Acts 15:5|Ac 15:5⟧; c. acc. rei, ⟦1 Corinthians 11:17|I Co 11:17⟧, ⟦2 Thessalonians 3:4|II Th 3:4⟧, ⟦1 Timothy 4:11|I Ti 4:11⟧ ⟦1 Timothy 5:7|5:7⟧; seq. ἵνα (M, Pr., 207; Bl., § 69, 4), ⟦Mark 6:8|Mk 6:8⟧, ⟦2 Thessalonians 3:12|II Th 3:12⟧; c. dat. pers., ⟦Acts 17:30|Ac 17:30⟧ R, txt., ⟦1 Thessalonians 4:11|I Th 4:11⟧; seq. λέγων, ⟦Matthew 10:5|Mt 10:5⟧; c. inf. aor., ⟦Matthew 15:35|Mt 15:35⟧, ⟦Mark 8:6|Mk 8:6⟧, ⟦Luke 8:29|Lk 8:29⟧, ⟦Acts 10:42|Ac 10:42⟧ ⟦Acts 16:18|16:18⟧ (aoristic pres.; v. M, Pr., 119); id. c. neg., μή, ⟦Luke 5:14|Lk 5:14⟧ ⟦Luke 8:56|8:56⟧, ⟦Acts 23:22|Ac 23:22⟧, ⟦1 Corinthians 7:10|I Co 7:10⟧; c. inf. pres., ⟦Acts 16:23|Ac 16:23⟧, ⟦2 Thessalonians 3:6|II Th 3:6⟧; id. c. neg., μή, ⟦Luke 9:21|Lk 9:21⟧, ⟦Acts 1:4|Ac 1:4⟧ ⟦Acts 4:18|4:18⟧ ⟦Acts 5:28|5:28⟧, ⟦Acts 5:40|40⟧, ⟦1 Timothy 1:3|I Ti 1:3⟧ ⟦1 Timothy 6:17|6:17⟧; c. acc., τοῦτο, seq. ὅτι (B1., § 70, 3), ⟦2 Thessalonians 3:10|II Th 3:10⟧; c. acc. et inf., ⟦Acts 23:30|Ac 23:30⟧, ⟦2 Thessalonians 3:6|II Th 3:6⟧, ⟦1 Timothy 6:13|I Ti 6:13⟧ (Bl., § 72, 5).†
SYN.: v.s. ἐντέλλω.
a: A Grammar of N.T. Greek. Vol. I, Prolegomena, by J. H. Moulton. Third Edition. Scribners, 1908

G3854.b:
⟪παρα-γίνομαι⟫
(Ion. and late for -γίγν-), [in LXX chiefly for ⁨בּוֹא⁩;]
⟪1.⟫ ⟪to be beside⟫ or ⟪at hand⟫ (Hom., Hdt., al.), hence, ⟪to stand by⟫, ⟪support⟫ (Æsch., Thuc., al.): c. dat. pers., ⟦2 Timothy 4:16|II Ti 4:16⟧.
⟪2.⟫ ⟪to come⟫, ⟪come up⟫, ⟪arrive⟫ (Hdt., Xen., al., and freq. in later writers; v. MM, xviii; Thackeray, Gr., 2672): absol., ⟦Luke 14:21|Lk 14:21⟧ ⟦Luke 19:16|19:16⟧, ⟦John 3:23|Jo 3:23⟧, ⟦Acts 5:21|Ac 5:21⟧, ⟦Acts 5:22|22⟧, ⟦Acts 5:25|25⟧ ⟦Acts 9:39|9:39⟧ ⟦Acts 10:32|10:32⟧, ⟦Acts 10:33|33⟧ ⟦Acts 11:23|11:23⟧ ⟦Acts 14:27|14:27⟧ ⟦Acts 17:10|17:10⟧ ⟦Acts 18:27|18:27⟧ ⟦Acts 21:18|21:18⟧ ⟦Acts 23:16|23:16⟧, ⟦Acts 23:35|35⟧ ⟦Acts 24:17|24:17⟧, ⟦Acts 24:24|24⟧ ⟦Acts 25:7|25:7⟧ ⟦Acts 28:21|28:21⟧, ⟦1 Corinthians 16:3|I Co 16:3⟧; seq. εἰς, ⟦John 8:2|Jo 8:2⟧, ⟦Acts 9:26|Ac 9:26⟧ ⟦Acts 15:4|15:4⟧; ἐπί, c. acc., ⟦Luke 22:52|Lk 22:52⟧; πρός, c. acc., ⟦Luke 7:4|Lk 7:4⟧, ⟦Luke 7:20|20⟧ ⟦Luke 8:19|8:19⟧, ⟦Acts 20:18|Ac 20:18⟧; id. seq. ἐκ, ⟦Luke 11:6|Lk 11:6⟧; παρά, c. gen., ⟦Mark 14:43|Mk 14:43⟧; ἀπὸ . . . εἰς, ⟦Matthew 2:1|Mt 2:1⟧, ⟦Acts 13:14|Ac 13:14⟧; ἀπὸ . . . ἐπὶ . . . πρός, ⟦Matthew 3:13|Mt 3:13⟧; of a teacher coming forward in public: ⟦Matthew 3:1|Mt 3:1⟧, ⟦Luke 12:51|Lk 12:51⟧, ⟦Hebrews 9:11|He 9:11⟧.†
a: A Grammar of the O.T. in Greek I, by H. St. J. Thackeray. Cambridge, 1909

G3855.b:
⟪παρ-άγω⟫,
[in LXX chiefly for ⁨עבר⁩;]
⟪1.⟫ trans., ⟪to lead by⟫, ⟪lead aside⟫, ⟪lead into⟫, ⟪lead forward⟫, etc.
⟪2.⟫ Intrans.,
	⟪(a)⟫ ⟪to pass by⟫: ⟦Matthew 9:9|Mt 9:9⟧, ⟦Matthew 9:27|27⟧ ⟦Matthew 20:30|20:30⟧, ⟦Mark 2:14|Mk 2:14⟧ ⟦Mark 15:21|15:21⟧, ⟦John 8:59|Jo 8:59⟧ R, txt., ⟦John 9:1|9:1⟧; seq. παρό, c. acc., ⟦Mark 1:16|Mk 1:16⟧;
	⟪(b)⟫ ⟪to go away⟫, ⟪depart⟫; metaph., ⟪to pass away⟫: ⟦1 Corinthians 7:31|I Co 7:31⟧; mid., ⟦1 John 2:8|I Jo 2:8⟧, ⟦1 John 2:17|17⟧.†

G3856.b:
† ⟪παρα-δειγματίζω⟫
(< δείκνυμι), [in LXX: ⟦Numbers 25:4|Nu 25:4⟧ (⁨יקע⁩ hi.), ⟦Jeremiah 13:22|Je 13:22⟧ (⁨חמס⁩ ni.), ⟦Ezekiel 28:17|Ez 28:17⟧ (⁨רַאֲוָה⁩), ⟦Ezra 4:17|Es 4:17⟧, ⟦Daniel 2:5|Da LXX 2:5⟧*;] ⟪to set forth as an example⟫; in bad sense, ⟪to put to open shame⟫: ⟦Hebrews 6:6|He 6:6⟧ (Polyb., Plut., al.).†

G3857.b:
⟪παράδεισος⟫, -ου, ὁ
